question: A patient on clozapine develops fever, sore throat, and a WBC of 2,100/mm³ with neutrophils 800/mm³. What is the appropriate action?

answers.text: Stop clozapine immediately — this is agranulocytosis; the patient must never be rechallenged with clozapine

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Agranulocytosis (WBC <3,000 or neutrophils <1,500) is a life-threatening adverse effect of clozapine (~1–2% incidence). The drug must be stopped permanently — rechallenge carries extreme risk of fatal recurrence. Supportive care includes G-CSF, infection management, and switching to an alternative antipsychotic.

answers.text: Reduce clozapine dose by 50% and add prophylactic antibiotics — dose-dependent neutropaenia will resolve

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Clozapine-induced agranulocytosis is not reliably dose-dependent and cannot be managed by dose reduction. Once neutrophils fall below 1,500/mm³, the drug must be stopped completely. Continuing at any dose risks fatal sepsis from severe neutropaenia.

answers.text: Continue clozapine but increase WBC monitoring to weekly — transient leucopaenia is common and self-limiting

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Mild leucopaenia (WBC 3,000–3,500) may warrant increased monitoring and continuation. But this patient has agranulocytosis (WBC 2,100, neutrophils 800) — this is a medical emergency, not a transient finding. Continuation risks fatal infection.

answers.text: Switch to haloperidol and add G-CSF — haloperidol never causes blood dyscrasias

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Stopping clozapine is correct, but haloperidol is not the ideal substitute for a patient who was on clozapine (which is reserved for treatment-resistant schizophrenia). The error in this option is the claim that haloperidol never causes dyscrasias — while rare, it can. More importantly, the patient needs an alternative atypical with efficacy in resistant disease.

overallFeedback.feedback: Clozapine's unique efficacy in treatment-resistant schizophrenia comes with the unique risk of agranulocytosis (~1–2%). The absolute rule: WBC <3,000 or neutrophils <1,500 → stop clozapine immediately, never rechallenge.

Clozapine-induced agranulocytosis requires immediate permanent discontinuation. This is why all clozapine patients must be registered for mandatory haematological monitoring (weekly WBC for 18 weeks, then fortnightly). The risk makes clozapine a last-resort drug for treatment-resistant schizophrenia only.
